samples.summary: Read-only editor test's store spies can never fire — the new `changeFilter` and `EditorState.readOnly` layers are not isolated by any assertion
samples.evidence: `initialize()` now wraps the store in `readOnlyNoteStore()` (editor.ts:249) *before* anything touches it, so the `vi.spyOn(store,'editText')`/`vi.spyOn(store,'undo')` methods are replaced by the proxy's `noop`/`noHistory` on every access. `expect(editText).not.toHaveBeenCalled()` and `expect(undo).not.toHaveBeenCalled()` (editor.test.ts:56-57) are therefore true no matter what the view does. The remaining live assertion, `api.getText() === 'hello'`, is satisfied by `EditorState.readOnly` alone (all six calls go through `@codemirror/commands`-style commands that decline on a read-only state), so deleting the newly-added `EditorState.changeFilter.of(tr => tr.annotation(Transaction.remote))` (editor.ts:~462) would leave the whole suite green. No test dispatches a raw non-remote transaction (`view.dispatch({changes: …})`) to pin the filter itself.

samples.summary: `canUndo`/`canRedo` read-only gating asserted against a store that reports false anyway
samples.evidence: The diff changes `canUndo: () => !readOnly && store.canUndo()` (editor.ts:672). The only assertions are `expect(api.canUndo()).toBe(false)` / `canRedo` on a fresh `MemNoteStore('hello')` whose undo/redo stacks are empty (memory.ts:189-195) — and whose writes were all neutered anyway. The assertions hold identically with the `!readOnly &&` removed, so the new gating (which decides whether a host toolbar offers enabled undo/redo buttons on a viewer mount) has no coverage. A store seeded with history, or a stub whose `canUndo()` returns true, would be needed.

samples.summary: `setLocalSelection` and `recordSelectionForHistory` neutering is unverified despite the test being named "neuters every write path"
samples.evidence: read-only.test.ts:36-46 calls `view.setLocalSelection(1,2)` and `view.recordSelectionForHistory(...)` but asserts nothing about them; both only touch `MemNoteStore`'s private `currentSelection`/`batchAfterSelection`, which no assertion in the file observes (`store.getText()`/`store.canUndo()` are unaffected by either). The test passes unchanged if `setLocalSelection` were added to `NOTE_STORE_READERS` and forwarded — yet the wrapper's doc (read-only.ts:140-142) calls out publishing a viewer's caret as a deliberate `doc.update` to suppress. A spy-backed fake `NoteStore` (or asserting on a `subscribePresence`-observable effect) would pin it. `subscribePresence` forwarding is likewise unasserted.

samples.summary: Divider resize behaviour changed (25px hit area, `touch-action`, `track = rect.width - divider.offsetWidth`) with no test at all
samples.evidence: The drag-ratio math changed from `/ rect.width` to `/ (rect.width - divider.offsetWidth)` and the divider grew from 7px to 25px. Grepping `divider|splitRatio|pointerdown|offsetWidth` across packages/notes/src returns hits only in editor.ts — no test file mounts the split mode and dispatches a pointerdown/pointermove to assert the resulting `flex` basis. An off-by-a-divider-width regression (or a clamp mistake at 0.15/0.85) would ship unnoticed; jsdom reports `offsetWidth === 0`, so a naive test would also need a stub, which is exactly why this deserves a deliberate one.

samples.summary: The frontend mount's own `readOnlyNoteStore` wrap has no test
samples.evidence: notes-view.tsx now does `const store = readOnly ? readOnlyNoteStore(raw) : raw`. There is no `notes-view.test.tsx` (glob of packages/frontend/src/app/notes/*.test.tsx returns only notes-toolbar.test.tsx), and the new shared-notes-layout test mocks `@/app/notes/notes-view` away entirely, so nothing exercises this branch — including the inverse (that an editor mount is NOT wrapped, which would silently make the whole editor read-only). The engine wrap in `initialize()` is a redundant second layer, so a defect here is contained, but the un-wrapped direction is not covered anywhere.

samples.summary: "No localStorage writes" is only pinned for viewMode, not for keymap or showAuthors
samples.evidence: The layout's docblock claims "minus every `localStorage` write" and it wires `onKeymapChange={setKeymap}` / `onShowAuthorsChange={setShowAuthors}` (shared-notes-layout.tsx:108-111). Only the view-mode path has a non-persistence assertion (test line ~186 checks `wafflebase:notes:viewMode` is unchanged). Toggling the keymap or blame gutter through the toolbar menu is untested for both application and non-persistence, so a later change to `writeKeymap`/`writeShowAuthors` here would go unnoticed.

samples.summary: Layout tests mock out `NotesView`, so toolbar↔editor wiring is asserted only as prop-passing
samples.evidence: `vi.mock("@/app/notes/notes-view")` replaces the view with a props recorder plus a fully stubbed `NoteEditorAPI` in which every command is `vi.fn()` and every capability returns true. The tests therefore prove buttons render and props flow, not that a click reaches a real editor command. That is a reasonable trade for a CodeMirror+Yorkie mount, but note that no test asserts a toolbar button actually invokes the corresponding `NoteEditorAPI` method on this route (e.g. clicking Bold → `toggleBold`), so a mis-wired `editor` prop would still pass.
